content.text:
In this branch we've added a CLI for our Jenkins-based CI. The CLI has several layers, from highest to lowest being: 
- ../gkylsoft/gkeyll/bin/gkeyll jeci
- ./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh
- ./ci/jenkins/jenkins-<machine>.sh

One thing I frequently want to examine is the Jenkins console output. Could that be stored as an artifact or retreived some other way through the CLI? Ideally it'd be stored as an artifact and I could use the "fetch" command to download it. Alternatively we could add a new command, or a new flag to an existing command, to retreive it.
I’ll trace the existing `jeci` command path and its artifact-fetch plumbing, then add console-output retrieval in the layer that keeps the CLI behavior coherent.

I’m adding `artifact --fetch --console`, which saves Jenkins’ retained `consoleText` as `jenkins-console.txt` alongside downloaded artifacts. This avoids relying on Pipeline-internal log-file access and also works for builds created before this change.

Implemented console retrieval through the existing artifact fetch command:

```sh
gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu artifact --build 187 --fetch --console
```

This downloads Jenkins’ retained `consoleText` as:

```text
gkeyll-ci-build-187/jenkins-console.txt
```

It can be combined with normal artifact selection:

```sh
gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu artifact --build 187 --fetch --console \
  --only ci-regression-summary.txt
```

- Shown under the build’s **Artifacts** section in the Jenkins browser.
- Available at the usual `/artifact/jenkins-console.txt` URL.
- Listed by `gkeyll jeci … artifact --build 187`.
- Downloadable with the existing `--fetch --only jenkins-console.txt`.

content.text:
`archiveArtifacts` can only archive files in the agent workspace; Jenkins’ console log lives on the controller. `currentBuild.rawBuild` is the direct bridge: the Pipeline copies that controller-side log into `jenkins-console.txt`, then archives it normally.

The tradeoff is Jenkins Script Security. A job running in the Groovy sandbox may reject that controller API until an administrator approves it; a reviewed, non-sandbox Pipeline can use it directly. The benefit is exactly the behavior you want—browser-visible, ordinary artifact, with no plugin or CLI special case. The snapshot will include all test/stage output up to the archival step, but not the few final Jenkins lines emitted while archiving/cleaning up.

questions.question: Should the plan use `currentBuild.rawBuild` and explicitly verify/approve it on each Jenkins controller if its Pipeline sandbox blocks the call?

options.label: Yes, use rawBuild (Recommended)
options.description: Keeps the feature self-contained and creates `jenkins-console.txt` as a normal artifact.

options.label: No, avoid it
options.description: The plan will require a separate Jenkins plugin or controller-side mechanism instead.

content.text:
<proposed_plan>
# Archive Jenkins console output as a normal artifact

## Summary

Replace the endpoint-based `--console` fetch feature with a real `jenkins-console.txt` artifact for every newly run CI build. It will appear in Jenkins’ browser artifact list and work with the existing `artifact --list` and `artifact --fetch --only` interface.

## Implementation changes

- First restore all seven files changed by the prior `--console` implementation to commit `669081e6e15ba3f0c0f60622a9fcff10e4a69001`:
  - `ci/jenkins/jenkins-client-artifacts.sh`
  - `ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh`
  - all four `jenkins-<machine>.sh` clients
  - `ci/jenkins/README.md`
- Do not retain `--console`, `/consoleText` helpers, or any special-case CLI behavior.
- In the three actual archive-owning Pipelines—`jenkinsfile.personal`, `Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu`, and `Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu`—add a small helper that reads the current build’s controller-side log via `currentBuild.rawBuild`, writes it to workspace file `jenkins-console.txt`, and invokes it immediately before the existing `archiveArtifacts` call.
  - The snapshot includes all CI output up through timing/failure-summary generation.
  - Add `jenkins-console.txt` to each existing artifact glob/list.
  - Treat failure to create or archive the snapshot as an archival failure, consistent with the current artifact behavior.
  - The team-workstation CI needs no separate archival edit: its trusted workflow loads `jenkinsfile.personal`.
- Update the CI README after restoration to document that `jenkins-console.txt` is a standard artifact, e.g.:
  ```sh
  gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu artifact --build 187 --fetch --only jenkins-console.txt
  ```
  It will also be included by an unfiltered `--fetch`.

## Test plan

- Confirm the restored CLI/client files contain no `--console` option or `consoleText` endpoint handling.
- Run shell syntax checks and existing CLI help checks; verify artifact help returns to its original interface.
- On a staging build for each controller type, verify:
  - Jenkins’ build page lists `jenkins-console.txt` under **Artifacts**.
  - `artifact --build N` lists it with the other archived files.
  - `artifact --build N --fetch --only jenkins-console.txt` downloads it successfully.
  - Its contents include normal stage/test output and the expected failure output on a deliberately failing build.
- If Jenkins Script Security blocks `currentBuild.rawBuild`, have the controller administrator approve the specific reviewed Pipeline call, then rerun the staging build.

## Assumptions

- The reviewed Pipelines may use `currentBuild.rawBuild`; administrator approval is acceptable if a controller’s Groovy sandbox requires it.
- Console artifacts are available for builds created after this change. Retained historical builds will continue to expose their console only through Jenkins’ normal console view.
</proposed_plan>
Implement the plan.

I’ll remove the endpoint-specific CLI changes first, then add the normal Jenkins artifact snapshot at each Pipeline’s existing archival point. The team-workstation job inherits the personal Pipeline, so the implementation needs three Pipeline edits rather than four.

Implemented the artifact-native approach.

- Restored all endpoint/`--console` CLI changes; the normal artifact interface is unchanged.
- Each Pipeline now snapshots its Jenkins log as `jenkins-console.txt` immediately before `archiveArtifacts`, so it appears in Jenkins’ browser artifact list and works with:
  ```sh
  gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu artifact --build 187 --fetch --only jenkins-console.txt
  ```
- Updated [README.md](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/README.md:40).
- Added the snapshot/archive logic to [jenkinsfile.personal](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/jenkinsfile.personal:252), [Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu:557), and [Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu:555). Team-workstation inherits the personal Pipeline.

The snapshot uses Jenkins’ `getLogReader()` API, which avoids the deprecated file-backed log API. [Jenkins API docs](https://javadoc.jenkins.io/hudson/model/Run.html)

Validated shell syntax, CLI help restoration, targeted baseline restoration, and `git diff --check`. A Jenkins staging build remains needed to approve `currentBuild.rawBuild` if Script Security requests it and to verify browser artifact visibility.
1. Will this work with all 4 machines (personal/stellar_cpu/perlmutter_gpu/team) ?2. Will this work with Jenkins runs prior to this change?

1. Yes. Personal, Stellar, and Perlmutter archive it directly; team-workstation runs the trusted personal Pipeline, so it gets the same artifact.

2. No. Only builds run after this Pipeline change will contain `jenkins-console.txt`. Older retained builds still have their normal Jenkins console page, but it will not appear in their artifact list or be fetchable as an artifact.
Is there another, existing way to see the console via CLI?

Yes: the existing `follow` command streams a known build’s Jenkins console:

```sh
gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu follow --build 187
```

It works for all four platforms and can also resolve a queue ID:

```sh
gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu follow --queue 42
```

For a completed retained build, it replays the available console output and then reports the final status. It does not save the output locally or make it an artifact.
